features.description: Consumer-family taxonomy + evidence vocabulary. Map the existing 8 qa-sufficiency surface classes into two families (human, agent); add a consumer dimension to the journey model. Add a SINGLE CLOSED evidence_class enum plus a data_provenance marker as NEW optional fields on EvidenceRef WITHOUT inventing new EvidenceRef.type enum values: each evidence_class maps to a valid existing type, and data_provenance is one of seeded|real|degraded. Also add two structured fields to EvidenceRef so degradation/typed-skip and keyed cross-surface comparison are STRUCTURAL not prose: data_source (a stable key) and availability (available|unavailable). A typed-skip is represented as availability=unavailable + data_provenance=degraded — data_provenance is NOT extended with a skip value (D017).
features.acceptance: A pure module defines a CLOSED surface_class enum and SurfaceFamily. The surface_class enum is the canonical structural set derived from the 8 qa-sufficiency surface classes (D024): {read_only_ui, interactive_ui, mobile_app, cli_human, agent_mcp_tool, cli_agent, external_integration, service_batch}. The legacy qa class 'mutation' is NOT a surface_class — it is modeled as claim_kind=mutation (D014); 'command (CLI)' splits into cli_human (human operator) vs cli_agent (the agent CLI transcript F003 captures); 'agent / MCP tool' is agent_mcp_tool; 'service / batch (backend/API)' is service_batch. A documented table maps each legacy-8 class AND each journey.surfaces token (web, backend, mcp_tool, cli_agent, cli_human) to a surface_class; the enum is closed (unknown surface_class rejected). SurfaceFamily (human, agent) has a total, tested mapping from every surface_class member to exactly one family. The objective_contract UserJourney gains consumer (human|agent|both) — REQUIRED for any journey asserting a consumer-facing outcome (omission rejected for such journeys; D030) — and fixture_only (bool, DEFAULT false; D031). Unknown consumer values are rejected. CONSUMER x SURFACE validation (D026): a journey with consumer=human must declare >=1 human-family surface, consumer=agent >=1 agent-family surface, consumer=both >=1 of EACH; a mismatch is rejected so required-evidence derivation is unambiguous. EvidenceRef VALIDATION (D027): availability may be set only together with data_source (an availability without a data_source key is rejected). EvidenceRef gains, in the agent-conventions schema + Pydantic model + validator (with a VERSION bump): (a) evidence_class — a SINGLE CLOSED enum defined once and referenced by F002/F003/F004, covering human {screenshot, recording, journey_walk, terminal_transcript, rubric, human_signoff}, agent {tool_call_transcript, cli_transcript, contract_check}, mutation {idempotency, rollback}, structured {structured_error}; (b) data_provenance (seeded|real|degraded); (c) data_source (optional str key); (d) availability (optional, available|unavailable); (e) consumer_family (optional, human|agent) — explicit source-family attribution so F004 cross-family comparison never infers family from evidence_class (which breaks for shared classes like structured_error) (D037). The EvidenceRef.type enum is NOT extended (test asserts the 8 existing type values are unchanged) and a documented table maps each evidence_class to a valid existing type. Tests cover the total surface->family mapping, consumer validation, the new optional fields parsing, the closed-enum invariant (no evidence_class outside the set is accepted), the typed-skip representation (availability=unavailable + data_provenance=degraded, no new provenance value), and the no-new-type-value invariant.

features.description: Evidence-class typing rule. Pure function from a claim's (surface_class, consumer, claim_kind) to the required evidence_class(es) drawn ONLY from F001's closed enum, plus a checker that matches a claim's evidence by evidence_class AND data_provenance. claim_kind (read_only|mutation|qualitative) is a separate dimension from surface_class because mutation and qualitative are claim kinds, not surfaces, and may share a surface with read-only claims (D014). Seeded evidence does not satisfy a consumer-readiness claim unless the journey is fixture_only. Mismatch is advisory (warn) at implementation time; close-time blocking is OUT OF SCOPE here — the sibling enforcement plan 2b (2026-06-15-002) consumes this typing result and decides blocking (D040).
features.acceptance: required_evidence_classes(surface_class, consumer, claim_kind) is pure and returns a REQUIREMENT EXPRESSION over F001's closed evidence_class enum with EXPLICIT set semantics (D020): the result is a list of requirement groups; each group is satisfied by ANY ONE of its alternatives (written a|b|c = at-least-one-of), and ALL groups must be satisfied (groups are conjunctive). Example: read_only_ui human -> [ {screenshot|recording|journey_walk} ] (one group, any one); agent_mcp_tool read_only SUCCESS -> [ {tool_call_transcript|contract_check} ] (a successful tool-call or contract transcript alone satisfies); structured_error is required ONLY for an error-path claim, signalled by claim_kind=error_path (claim_kind is extended to {read_only, mutation, qualitative, error_path}; D033) -> adds the group [{structured_error}] (D028). It is NOT unconditionally conjunctive. Concretely: cli_human read_only -> [{terminal_transcript}]; cli_agent read_only -> [{cli_transcript}]; claim_kind=mutation adds TWO separate conjunctive groups [{idempotency},{rollback}] — BOTH idempotency AND rollback required (D035) — on top of the surface/consumer base; JOURNEY-LEVEL AGGREGATION (D033): a journey declares surfaces[] and one consumer; required evidence is the UNION of the per-(surface, claim_kind) groups over all declared surfaces, and for consumer=both the aggregate MUST include >=1 human-family-surface requirement AND >=1 agent-family-surface requirement, satisfied together; claim_kind=qualitative -> [{rubric|human_signoff}]. The evidence_class names are EXACTLY F001's enum (contract_check, not contract_test; terminal_transcript for cli_human vs cli_transcript for agent CLI are distinct). A checker, given a claim's (surface_class, consumer, claim_kind) + its evidence (evidence_class + data_provenance), returns satisfied | evidence_class_mismatch (names the missing class) | seeded_masks_readiness (a required class is present but only with data_provenance=seeded while the journey is not fixture_only). Tests: (1) UI read_only claim with only test_output -> evidence_class_mismatch; (2) UI claim with a real screenshot -> satisfied; (3) UI claim satisfied only by a seeded screenshot on a non-fixture_only journey -> seeded_masks_readiness; (4) same on a fixture_only journey -> satisfied; (5) a mutation claim on a UI surface requires idempotency+rollback in addition to the read_only base. The function is pure (no I/O, no input mutation).

features.description: Agent-surface evidence class in the runtime-evidence harness. Three dogfoodable EvidenceSource adapters reusing harness.py Protocol composition and the evidence/goal-governance/post_impl/<source>/<journey>/ convention: (a) CLI non-interactive transcript, (b) MCP tool-call transcript driving DontPanic's own in-process mcp_server (tools/list + a read-only tool), (c) schema/contract-stability check. Each sets an evidence_class drawn from F001's closed agent set + a valid EXISTING EvidenceRef.type + data_provenance, with honest typed-skip represented per D017.
features.acceptance: Three new EvidenceSource adapters register with the harness; each returns list[EvidenceRef] whose type is a valid EXISTING enum value (e.g. log for transcripts, test_output for the contract check, file for artifacts), whose evidence_class is the F001 closed agent vocabulary (tool_call_transcript | cli_transcript | contract_check), and whose data_provenance is set. Artifacts land under evidence/goal-governance/post_impl/<source>/<journey>/. The MCP source invokes the in-process mcp_server (tools/list + one read-only tool e.g. list_projects or status) and records request+response with no secret-shaped field. When a prerequisite is absent, the source emits a typed-skip EvidenceRef represented as availability=unavailable + data_provenance=degraded (NO new provenance value; D017) carrying an operator-readable reason in EvidenceRef.note (and, for transcript/log sources, the same reason in the artifact body) — the reason location is explicit and asserted, not opaque (D029). A harness test runs all three against a fixture journey and asserts artifacts + the source-agnostic invariant (dispatch by registration, never hardcoded source name). No live paid call is made: the CLI source runs a pinned NON-INTERACTIVE, read-only command under a fixture/offline env guard (no network, no paid external execution); its command contract (argv + exit code + stdout schema) is fixed and asserted (D039).

features.description: Per-family degraded honesty + structured cross-surface agreement. Add required_data_sources and allowed_degraded_modes (keyed by a shared data-source key, e.g. capability id) to the journey contract. A checker verifies degradation is honest per family and that a typed-skip counts as honest-unavailability evidence rather than journey success, and that human and agent journeys for the same objective agree on capability-availability/provenance compared by the shared key. ALL comparison reads the STRUCTURED EvidenceRef fields introduced in F001 (data_source, availability, data_provenance) — never prose (D012).
features.acceptance: The UserJourney contract accepts required_data_sources[] (each with a stable data_source key) and allowed_degraded_modes[]. Evidence records availability per source structurally on EvidenceRef (F001): an agent capability_unavailable signal IS an agent EvidenceRef with data_source=<key> + availability=unavailable; an honest human label IS a human EvidenceRef with data_source=<key> + availability=unavailable. A pure checker, reading {data_source, availability, data_provenance} off the EvidenceRefs keyed by data_source, reports: (1) degraded_dishonest evaluated PER REQUIRED FAMILY: for each required data_source, EACH consumer_family the journey requires must itself carry an honest availability=unavailable EvidenceRef for that key when the source is down — one family masking (omitting its unavailable signal) while the other degrades is degraded_dishonest, NOT honest (a 'neither family' test is insufficient) (D036); additionally a degraded EvidenceRef is honest ONLY if its mode is listed in the journey's allowed_degraded_modes for that data_source, else degraded_dishonest (D038); (2) that a typed-skip EvidenceRef (availability=unavailable + data_provenance=degraded) for a data_source is treated as honest-unavailability evidence and NEVER as a satisfying consumer-surface capture (test asserts a journey 'covered' only by typed-skips is not satisfied); (3) cross_surface_disagreement when the human and agent EvidenceRefs for the SAME data_source key assert different availability or data_provenance (comparison on the structured fields, not description text). The typed-skip-vs-honest-degradation discriminator is at the journey EVIDENCE-SET level, not the tuple (D023): the same {availability=unavailable, data_provenance=degraded} EvidenceRef is honest-unavailability either way; a journey is satisfied only when its evidence set ALSO contains a real (non-seeded) journey-EXECUTION EvidenceRef — a set of only unavailable/typed-skip tuples is unsatisfied. Tests cover honest-degradation pass, degraded_dishonest, typed-skip-not-success, the discriminator (same unavailable tuple, with vs without a real execution EvidenceRef -> satisfied vs not), and a keyed UI-promises-available vs API-says-unavailable disagreement. Pure, no I/O.
